note: From the guide-tone lines to a line of the singer's own over a ii-V-I: the two lines sung with eyes closed, then turns and short runs that join one guide tone to the next, then a free line over a bossa that lands on {{3}} or {{7}} as the last chord arrives. Key and tempo are moves (the faster stages and the second key of the old files), the bossa keeps its distance above the ballad, and the line about another key opens with {{?key}}.

exercise.title: ii-V-I guide tones, your way
exercise.why: Guide tones are the notes your ear checks a chord by, so once you can sing them without the staff, any line you make up has somewhere to start and somewhere to land.

cells.text: {{chord:ii7}} is the 2nd chord of the key, built on {{2}}. {{chord:V7}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}, and {{chord:Imaj7}} is the 1st, built on {{1}}.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, at {{=bpm}}. Sing the two guide-tone lines, one note per chord: {{4}}, {{4}}, {{3}}, then {{1}}, {{7}}, {{7}}. Sing them on "ah".
Then close your eyes and sing them again.
Practice until you hear each change coming before its chord box lights.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the backing track. As each chord arrives, put a turn on its ringed note: up to the note above, down to the note below, then hold it. Sing the held notes on "oo".
Then, at the end of a bar, run by step to one of the next chord's ringed notes, so you land as the chord changes. Sing the runs on "ah".
If a run lands late, shorten it to three notes.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the backing track, now as a bossa. Make up a line over the first two chords, and sing it on any vowel. Whatever you sing, land on {{3}} as {{chord:Imaj7}} arrives, and hold it.
Then aim for {{7}} instead, and put one hard leap, such as a tritone or a 7th, somewhere in each round.
Once both landings come easily, sing whatever you hear and leave a bar empty now and then.
{{?key}}In another key the chords are new, and the ringed notes are the same numbers.
